types.label: Multiple Response (MRQ)
types.description: Two or more correct options; partial credit max(0, (right − wrong) / total correct) × marks.

types.label: True / False
types.description: One or more statements, each True or False; marks split per statement.

types.label: Fill in the Blanks
types.description: Blanks written as [answer] in the text; alternates, case sensitivity, optional word bank.

types.label: Match the Following
types.description: Pairs of Column I and Column II; Column II is shuffled on the paper.

types.label: One-Word Answer (VSA)
types.description: A very short answer: one word or term.

types.label: Assertion and Reasoning
types.description: Assertion (A) and Reason (R) with the four standard codes A–D.

types.label: Numerical
types.description: A calculation with a numeric answer, unit and tolerance.

types.label: Arrange in Order
types.description: Put steps or events in the correct sequence.

types.label: Short Answer
types.description: Two to three sentences; model answer and key points.

types.label: Long Answer
types.description: A detailed answer; model answer and marking points.

types.label: Descriptive / Essay
types.description: An open answer with a model answer and a marking rubric.

types.label: HOTS (Higher-Order Thinking)
types.description: An Analyse / Evaluate / Create question with a model answer.

types.label: Diagram-Based
types.description: Refers to a diagram: upload one, or the AI describes the diagram to draw and label.

types.label: Case-Based
types.description: A case followed by sub-questions of mixed types.

types.label: Scenario-Based
types.description: A real-life scenario followed by application sub-questions.

types.label: Passage-Based / Comprehension
types.description: A reading passage followed by comprehension sub-questions.

settings.ar_instruction: Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.
ar_codes: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
